questions.question: During the reign of which of the following Sultans of Delhi was actual power enjoyed by Balban?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **During the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud**, who was made Sultan by Balban in exchange for the positions of **Amiri-Hajib and Naib-i-mamlakat,** Balban was awarded the position of Amiri-Hajib and Naib-i-mamlakat.
 
• He was also awarded a royal canopy by the sultan, indicating Balban's power during Nasiruddin's reign.
 
• **Balban** was one of **Iltutmish's most efficient slaves**.
 
• The Mongols sold him as a slave, and in 1232 AD, Iltutmish bought him and appointed him as Khassadar after being pleased by his accomplishments.
 
• During Razia's reign, Balban held the office of Amir-i-shikar, and successive sultans bestowed upon him the Jagir of Rewari and Hansi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

 
• **Nasir ud din Mahmud Shah** was the Mamluk Sultanate's seventh ruler (Slave dynasty).
 
• The court historian **Minhaj-i-Siraj **wrote the **Tabaqat-i Nasiri**, which is dedicated to him.
 
• Shamsuddin Iltutmish was his father (as clearly mentioned by Minhaj in Tabaqat-i-Nasiri).
 
• At the early age of 17 or 18, he succeeded to the throne of the Delhi Sultanate after the chiefs deposed Ala-ud-din Masud, believing Masud had become a tyrant.

questions.question: Which of the following is the State Tree of Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mango**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mango **has been designated as the **official tree of Maharashtra**.
 
• It is an edible fruit that originated in the region between** northwestern Myanmar, Bangladesh, and the northeastern Asian republic of Bangladesh**.
 
• It is also India's national fruit.
 
• Mango is a tropical stone fruit produced by the Mangifera indica tree, which is said to have originated in the region between northern Myanmar, Bangladesh, and northeastern India.
 
• Since ancient times, M. indica has been cultivated throughout South and Southeast Asia, resulting in two types of current mango cultivars: "Indian type" and "Southeast Asian type." 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The state tree of **Rajasthan **(where it is known as Khejri), Western **Uttar Pradesh** (where it is known as Chhonkara), and **Telangana **(where it is known as **Jammi**) in India is Prosopis cineraria.
 
• **The Ashoka tree's flower **is the state flower of Odisha, India.
 
• The state tree of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh is the** banyan tree**.

questions.question: Who among the following leaders was NOT an accused in the Kakori Train Robbery case?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhagat Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kakori Train Robbery **occurred during the** Indian Independence Movement **against the** British Raj on August 9, 1925, in Kakori,** a village near Lucknow.
 
• **Hindustan Republican Association** organised the event (HRA).
 
• **Ram Prasad Bismil and Ashfaqullah Khan** of the HRA, which subsequently became the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association, planned the theft.
 
• The goal of this organisation was to carry out revolutionary activities against the British Empire in order to achieve independence. Bismil Khan, Rajendra Lahiri, Chandrashekhar Azad, Sachindra Bakshi, Keshab Chakravarty, Manmathnath Gupta, Mukundi Lal, Murari Lal Gupta, and Banwari Lal carried out the heist plan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

 
• **Bhagat Singh **was a charismatic Indian revolutionary who took part in the erroneous murder of a minor British police officer in reprisal for the killing of an Indian nationalist.
 
• **Thakur Roshan Singh** was an Indian revolutionary who was sentenced in the Bareilly shooting case during the Non-Cooperation Movement of 1921–22. He was born in the hamlet of Nabada in the Shahjahanpur region of Uttar Pradesh to a Rajput family.
 
• **Rajendra Nath Lahiri,** better known as Rajendra Lahiri, was an Indian revolutionary who masterminded the Kakori plot and the Dakshineshwar blast.
 
• **Ram Prasad Bismil** was an Indian poet, writer, and revolutionary who fought against the British Raj in the Mainpuri Conspiracy of 1918 and the Kakori Conspiracy of 1925.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Ramsar Wetland Site named Renuka Wetland located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ramsar Wetland Site** named **Renuka Wetland **is located in **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• ​**Renuka Wetland **is 37 kilometres northeast of Nahan, the administrative centre of the district Sirmaur in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• Renuka is a natural wetland in the Western Himalayas that has survived natural disasters and tectonic upheavals throughout geological history.
 
• A tiny stream flows into the lake from the lower Himalayan slopes that surround it.
 
• The lush sub-tropical forests cover these hillsides. Wetlands are rich in biodiversity and have religious significance.
 
• According to a faunal census, the Renuka area comprises 443 kinds of fauna ranging from protozoa to mammals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wetlands** are locations where water covers the soil or is present at or near the soil's surface throughout the year or for variable periods of time, including during the growing season.
 
• The types of plant and animal communities that live in and on the soil are mostly determined by water saturation (hydrology).
 
• Both aquatic and terrestrial animals can thrive in wetlands.
 
• The** Renuka Fair **is held in the **Sirmaur **district of **Himachal Pradesh.** It is held in the month of **November**.
 
• This Fair is organized to pay homage to Mother Renuka's huge sacrifice.
 
• The fair commemorates the annual meeting of **Parashuram **and **Renuka**.

questions.question: How many pollutants are included to measure Air Quality Index in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The National Air Quality Index (AQI)** reduces complex data on **eight pollutants to a single number (index value), **nomenclature, and colour.
 
• On October 17, 2014, the National Air Quality Index (AQI) was launched to provide information on air quality to the general public in an easily understandable format.
 
• Air quality is measured using eight pollutants:
 
 
• **Particulate Matter (size less than 10 µm) or (PM10), **
 
• **Particulate Matter (size less than 2.5 µm) or (PM2.5),**
 
• **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂),**
 
• **Sulphur Dioxide (SO₂),**
 
• **Carbon Monoxide (CO),**
 
• **Ozone (O₃),**
 
• **Ammonia (NH₃), and**
 
• **Lead (Pb)**
 
 
 
• It should be noted that in India, ambient air quality criteria are set independently for around 12 pollutants, including the eight that make up the Air Quality Index.
 
• Air quality is divided into six categories by the AQI. **Good, Satisfactory, Moderately polluted, Poor, Very Poor, and Severe **are the categories.

questions.question: Who among the following is credited with giving a theory of population growth in his work titled 'Essay on Population' (1798)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thomas Robert Malthus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thomas Robert Malthus **was a famous 18th-century British economist who wrote** "An Essay on the Principle of Population"** in 1798, which outlined his population increase philosophy.
 
• Malthus proposed that population increase would continue unless it was slowed or reversed by disease, hunger, war, or natural disaster.
 
• He is also recognized for establishing the **Malthusian growth model,** which is an exponential formula for forecasting population rise.
 
• An Essay on the Principle of Population was first published anonymously in 1798, but Thomas Robert Malthus was quickly identified as the author.
 
• The book predicted future challenges based on the assumption that the population would expand in a geometric progression (doubling every 25 years) while food production would increase in an arithmetic progression, leaving a gap that would result in famine unless birth rates were reduced.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Adam Smith** was a Scottish economist and philosopher who was a prominent figure during the Scottish Enlightenment and a pioneer of political economics.
 
• **Karl Heinrich Marx **was a German philosopher, economist, historian, sociologist, political theorist, journalist, and socialist revolutionary who lived from 1818 to 1883. The Communist Manifesto, published in 1848, and the three-volume Das Kapital are two of his most well-known works.
 
• **Friedrich Engels** was a revolutionary socialist and a German philosopher, historian, political theorist, and critic of political economy. Together with Karl Marx, Engels developed what is now known as Marxism.

questions.question: In terms of abundance of metals in Earth’s solid crust, which place does iron enjoy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Second__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iron** is the** earth's second most abundant meta**l (5.0 per cent). 
 
• **Aluminium **makes up around 8% of the Earth's crust, making it the most prevalent metal on the planet.
 
• It is, however, always found in combination with other elements and never in a pure condition.
 
• Alum and aluminium oxide are two of the most commonly encountered aluminium compounds.
 
• Iron is the** second most prevalent metal on the planet, **followed by calcium. 5.0 per cent iron and 3.6 per cent calcium, with** Na, K, Mg, and Ti **following closely behind.
 
• Because supernova nucleosynthesis makes it easy to make elements from carbon through iron, they are significantly more plentiful in the universe. Calcium in its pure form is extremely rare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The crust, mantle, and core** are the** three layers of the Earth**.
 
• Solid rocks and minerals make up the crust.
 
• The mantle, which is largely solid rocks and minerals but punctuated by pliable patches of semi-solid lava, lies under the crust.
 
• A heated, dense metal core exists at the Earth's core.

questions.question: Who among the following foreign travellers was appointed in the state service by Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ibn Battuta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ibn Battuta **was a** Moorish** wanderer who came to India during **Muhammad bin Tughlaq's rule**.
 
• His book **Rehla (The Travelogue)** sheds a lot of light on Muhammad-bin-reign Tughlaq's as well as India's geographical, economic, and social situations. He was named Delhi's chief Qazi.
 
• Ibn Battuta was an Arabized Berber Maghrebi scholar and explorer who travelled extensively in Afro-Eurasia, primarily in the Muslim world, covering more distance than any other explorer in pre-modern history, totalling around 117,000 kilometres, surpassing Zheng He's 50,000 kilometres and Marco Polo's 24,000 kilometres.
 
• From 1325 to 1351,** Mohammad ibn Tughlaq** was the Sultan of Delhi. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Between 1271 and 1295, Marco Emilio Polo,** a Venetian merchant, explorer, and writer, travelled through Asia on the Silk Road.
 
• **Al-Masudi **was an Arab traveller, historian, and geographer.
 
• During the early 15th century, **Niccol de' Conti **visited India and Southeast Asia, as well as potentially Southern China.

questions.question: Which of the following states has the largest catchment area of Godavari Basin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Maharashtra **has the **largest catchment area of the Godavari Basin.**
 
• **The basin's catchment area** is** 3,12,812 sq km**, with **Maharashtra accounting for 48.6%,** Telangana for 20%, Madhya Pradesh for 10%, Andhra Pradesh for 3.4 percent, Chhattisgarh for 10.9 percent, Odisha for 5.7 percent, and Karnataka for 1.4 percent.
 
• **The Godavari River** is the largest of India's peninsular rivers. Maharashtra is known for its early flows, and Godavari is equal to Ganga in Maharashtra.
 
• It rises to a height of 1,067 metres in the Western Ghats in **Thriambak Hills in Maharashtra's Nashik district.**
 
• It is the **largest of Peninsular India's east-flowing rivers and the country's second-largest river.**
 
• The Godavari basin drains around 9.5 percent of India's entire land area. 
 
• The Godavari basin is located within the Deccan plateau. Around 32% of the Godavari basin's size is in the 500-750 m elevation range.
 
• The Mahadeo Hills, which consist of a succession of tablelands ranging in elevation from 600 to 1200 metres, border the basin on the north.

questions.question: Nitin Menon, who was included in the Elite Panel of Umpires/Referees for 2020-21 by an international sports body, is professionally associated with :
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **For the 2020-21 season, India's Nitin Menon **has been named to **the International Cricket Council's Elite Panel of Umpires**, replacing **England's Nigel Llong**.
 
• The 36-year-old, who has officiated in** three Tests, 24 One-Day Internationals, and 16 Twenty-20 Internationals,** is only India's third member of the famous panel, following former captain Srinivas Venkatraghavan and Sundaram Ravi, who were both fired last year.
 
• Menon, who was formerly a member of the Emirates ICC International Panel of Umpires, was chosen by a selection panel that included ICC General Manager (Cricket) Geoff Allardice (Chairman), former player Sanjay Manjrekar, and match referees Ranjan Madugalle and David Boon. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **An umpire** is a person who, according to the Laws of Cricket, has the ability to make judgements about happenings on the cricket pitch.
 
• The umpire keeps a record of the deliveries and announces the end of an over in addition to making judgements about the legality of deliveries, appeals for wickets, and the overall legal conduct of the game.
 
• A cricket umpire should not be confused with a referee, who normally only officiates international matches and makes no decisions that impact the game's outcome.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India states that there shall be a President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 52**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 52 of the Constitution of India** states that there shall be a** President of India.**
 
• The President of India is the** Republic of India's head of state**. The President of India is the nominal head of the country's executive, legislative, and judicial branches, as well as the commander-in-chief of the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• The Indian President is the country's leader and is also known as the country's first citizen.
 
• He is a member of the Union Executive, whose provisions are dealt with in** Article 52-78**, which includes articles on the President (Article 52-62).
 
• The Indian President is the country's first citizen and a symbol of the country's unity, unity, and integrity.
 
• Along with the Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, and Attorney-General of India, he is a member of the Union Executive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• According to **Article 54 **of the Indian Constitution, the President is chosen by an Electoral College made up of elected members of both Houses of Parliament, as well as elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of all states, as well as the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the Union Territory of Puducherry.
 
• According to **Article 55 **of the Indian Constitution, "the scale of representation of the various States shall be uniform as far as practical at the election of the President."
 
• The Qualifications for Election as President are laid out in **Article 58** of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the metals listed in the options is the least reactive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gold**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The least reactive** metal is** gold**. The chemical element gold has the symbol Au and the atomic number 79.
 
• It is a bright, somewhat reddish yellow, dense, soft, malleable, and ductile metal in its purest form.
 
• **Gold** is a transition metal and a **group 11 element** chemically.
 
• **A Reactivity series** is an arrangement of metals in decreasing order of reactivity.
 
• In a displacement reaction, this series is used to assess if a given metal can displace another metal. 
 
• Based on their reactions with **water and dilute acids, the metals potassium, sodium, lithium, calcium, magnesium, zinc, iron, and copper** can be arranged in decreasing order of reactivity. **Iron **is **more reactive **than **copper**.
 
• Because iron has four unpaired shells in its three subshells, while copper only has one, according to the atomic structure. As a result, iron reacts more quickly than copper.

questions.question: In 1990, the Dinesh Goswami Committee was formed to make recommendations on:

__
 
• **In 1990, the Dinesh Goswami Committee** was formed to **make recommendations on electoral reforms**.
 
• It proposed giving political parties in-kind governmental money.
 
• It also suggested that a candidate should not be permitted to contest in more than two constituencies.
 
• **Dinesh Goswami** was a politician in India. In 1989, he served as the **Law and Justice Minister in the V.P. Singh government**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Electoral reform **is the modification of electoral systems to better the expression of public desires in election results.
 
• While the first three general elections in India were held a free and fairway, it is widely believed that the fourth general election in 1967 marked the beginning of a decline in standards.
 
• **The Fundamental Duties** are defined as all citizens' moral responsibility to contribute to the promotion of patriotism and the preservation of India's unity.
 
• Individuals and the nation are both affected by the duties outlined in Part IV–A of the Constitution.
 
• **Police reforms** strive to change police organizations' principles, culture, rules, and procedures.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India directs the State to secure a social order for the promotion of welfare of the people?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 38**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 38 of the Constitution of India **directs the State to secure a social order for the promotion of the welfare of the people.
 
• **The Indian Constitution **instructs the government to maintain a social order that promotes the people's welfare.
 
• In this regard, it contains the following provisions:

 
• The State must try to promote the welfare of the people by guaranteeing and safeguarding a social order in which social, economic, and political justice inform all aspects of national life as efficiently as possible.
 
• The State shall, in particular, aim to reduce income disparities and eradicate disparities in status, facilities, and opportunities, not just between individuals but also between groups of persons living in various places or working in different occupations.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 42** aims to provide for reasonable working conditions and maternity leave. "The State shall make measures for securing reasonable and humane working conditions and for maternity relief," it says.
 
• **Article 44** conforms to the Directive Principles of State Policy, which states that the state shall endeavour to provide a uniform civil code (UCC) for its citizens throughout India's territory.
 
• **Article 45 **deals with children's access to free and compulsory education. "Within 10 years of the commencement of this Constitution, the State shall endeavour to provide for free and compulsory education for all children until they finish the age of fourteen years," it says.​

questions.question: The mineral named ‘Calaverite’ is a telluride mineral containing :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**gold**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Calaverite,** also known as **gold telluride**, is a rare gold telluride, a metallic mineral with the **chemical formula AuTe₂, in which about 3% of the gold** is replaced by silver.
 
• In 1861, it was discovered in Calaveras County, California, and in 1868, it was named after the county.
 
• **The mineral's colour **can range from silvery white to brassy yellow and has a metallic shine.
 
• It is similar to the gold-silver telluride mineral sylvanite, although it contains substantially more silver.
 
• **Krennerite** is another AuTe₂ mineral with a distinct crystal structure.
 
• The principal gold telluride ores are calaverite and sylvanite, albeit such ores are often small gold sources.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gold** is a naturally occurring chemical element with the **symbol Au and atomic number 79**, making it one of the **higher atomic number elements**.
 
• In its pure state, it is a **bright, slightly orange-yellow, dense, soft, malleable, and ductile metal**.
 
• Gold is a transition metal and a group 11 element chemically. It is a non-reactive chemical element that is solid under normal conditions.
 
• In rocks, veins, and alluvial deposits, gold is frequently found in its free elemental (native) form as nuggets or grains.
 
• It can be found in solid solution with the native element silver (as electrum), naturally alloyed with other metals like copper and palladium, and mineral inclusions like pyrite.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Bhakti sect named 'Pushtimarg'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vallabhacharya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vallabhacharya** was **the founder of the Bhakti sect named 'Pushtimarg'**.
 
• **Pushtimarg** is a subtradition of Rudra Sampradaya, also known as Pushtimarg Sampradaya or Vallabha Sampradaya (Vaishnavism).
 
• Vallabhacharya (1479–1531) founded it in the early 16th century, and it is dedicated to Krishna.
 
• Pushtimarg, a bhakti (devotional) school, was expanded by Vallabhacharya's followers, particularly Gusainji.
 
• Its principles are rooted from, and its devotional practises are centred on, the fabled amorous plays of young Krishna, such as those described in the Bhagavata Purana and those associated with Govardhana Hill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vallabhacharya **is a Hindu Indian saint and philosopher who developed the Krishna-centered PushtiMarg Vaishnavism sect and the Shuddha Advaita Vedanta philosophy in the Braj area of India (Pure Non-dualism).
 
• **Adi Shankaracharya **was an Indian Vedic scholar and teacher whose works give a harmonising reading of the sastras, with liberating knowledge of the self at its core, combining Advaita Vedanta teachings of the period.
 
• **Kabir Das** was an Indian mystic poet and saint who wrote in the 15th century and impacted Hinduism's Bhakti movement. His lines can be found in Sikhism's scripture Guru Granth Sahib, Satguru Granth Sahib of Saint Garib Das, and Kabir Sagar. 
 
• **Ramanuja** was an Indian Hindu philosopher, guru, and social reformer, also known as Ramanujacharya.
